the_signal.headline: Event-driven architectures now mandatory for AI agent scaling
the_signal.body: n8n's deep dive on event-driven microservices reveals the production tradeoff GTM teams are hitting: synchronous workflows break under agent load, async patterns are non-negotiable. This is your operational blueprint when multi-agent coordination failures spike. Queue vs. stream decisions now directly impact your agent reliability SLA.

tool_drop.name: Replay QA for Teams
tool_drop.what: Records and replays test scenarios across team workflows for debugging automation failures.
tool_drop.why: When your AI workflows fail in production, replay-based debugging beats logs—gives you the exact state chain that broke your agent.

thread_of_day.title: RPA vs. Workflow Automation: Building Automation That Lasts
thread_of_day.takeaway: RPA dies when requirements shift; workflow automation with proper observability and governance scales through agent day-2 problems.

quote.text: Token prices won't increase if you host your own LLMs—providers are operating at a loss, subsidized by big tech.

whats_moving.context: As token arbitrage collapses, GTM teams realizing their cost models assumed unsustainable pricing; self-hosting becomes margin protection, not just infrastructure choice.
n8n flagging when CoT actually hurts agent performance—teams blindly chaining reasoning steps are wasting tokens and adding latency without accuracy gains.
Multi-agent systems hitting production reveals auth method choice (keys vs tokens vs OAuth) is now a reliability bottleneck, not just security hygiene.

act_on_this: Audit your multi-agent workflow for synchronous blocking calls—map them to event queues (not streams) and measure latency improvement before your next agent deployment.

numbers.stat: $12B wasted on a modeling mistake in PJM energy market
numbers.context: When AI/automation logic compounds errors across systems, small mistakes scale to massive costs—your observability and validation layers are now revenue-protection infrastructure.
